tracks.narration: Three programs are ready to run, but only one CPU. Who goes first — and for how long?
First in, first out runs each job to completion. Job A is long, so jobs B and C wait — and a quick keystroke in C can sit idle for seconds. That is starvation by queue order.
Round-robin fixes that. Pick a fixed time slice — say one unit — give it to the next ready job, then rotate. The queue keeps spinning while everyone makes progress.
Watch the Gantt chart fill up. A, B, C, A, B, C — every job gets the CPU within one tick of being ready. Response time becomes predictable.
A small slice feels snappy but spends time on context switches. A big slice runs efficiently but starts to look like FIFO. Picking the slice is the whole game.
